# Open questions — evidence-intake-project

What is not yet known, and what has since been answered.

## Open

### May a later pass append new segments to an already-imported source when the hash and length match exactly?

`open` · `@evidence-intake-project.ingest.append-to-identical-source-question/1`

import_normalized refuses an existing source id or hash so evidence is never silently replaced. That also means every extraction of a video (scenes, detections, captions, clock readings, soundtrack) must arrive in the one batch that first imports it; running the VLM or OCR a week later against a video already in the case has nowhere to land, which contradicts the overnight-job story. Appending segments (never touching the source row) when id, production, sha256 and byte_length all match and every segment id is new does not replace anything -- but it changes a stated invariant and needs a decision, a test that a differing hash or a reused segment id is still refused, and a look at what the case-isolation checks assume. Edges between existing sources are already possible without it (@evidence-intake-project.decision.adapters-may-propose-structural-edges).

### Who is the element re-assessment trail for?

`open` · `@evidence-intake-project.review.reassessment-trail-audience/1`

Changing an element assessment should leave a review trail rather than being refused, as it is today. Unresolved: is that trail user-facing — part of the defender's working record, shown in the element matrix and readable as 'I read this differently in March' — or an admin-facing audit log kept for accountability and not routinely surfaced? The answer decides whether re-assessment reuses `review_events` and `ReviewTarget` (user-facing, same vocabulary as every other decision, needing a new target kind and a trigger-enforced state check on element_links) or gets a separate append-only table with a different read path and different export rules. Element mappings are attorney analysis, so a user-facing trail is also privileged material and must stay out of any discovery export, which an admin-facing log might not need to be.

### Does anonymous within-clip tracking (track_n, no identity) belong in scope, or is it identity by another name?

`open` · `@evidence-intake-project.video.anonymous-tracking-question/1`

A tracker (ByteTrack/DeepSORT class) can say "the same figure appears at 0:12, 3:40 and 7:02" as track_3 without naming anyone, and a person could then author a possibly_same_person edge from track_3 to an entity with a rationale -- indexing, not identification, and structurally like SPEAKER_nn diarization. It is deferred, not excluded, because the payoff over text-to-frame retrieval ("find frames with a person") is modest and the temptation to let a track become an identity is real. Decide once retrieval and the deterministic slices exist: does a track add enough over retrieval to justify a machine-asserted "same figure" claim, and if so what keeps it from becoming an identity assertion (no re-identification across clips, no appearance embedding stored, track ids never exported)?

### Does the soundtrack ffmpeg extracts share the video stream's zero, or can a container's audio start_time shift every statement by a fixed delta?

`open` · `@evidence-intake-project.video.soundtrack-pts-offset-question/1`

merge_soundtrack proves both adapters hashed the same container, but not that the audio timeline the ASR saw is the video timeline the scene cutter saw. If a container carries a non-zero audio start_time (or the streams' PTS bases differ), evidence_audio::open_media's ffmpeg wav extraction may drop or shift the lead-in and every statement sits a fixed delta off the scenes while nothing notices. Resolve with an ffmpeg-guarded integration test: mux a clip with a known video-frame event and a beep at a known second, with a deliberate audio start_time offset, and assert the statement/scene locators agree; if they do not, `extract_wav` needs `-copyts`/`-start_at_zero` handling or an explicit offset carried into the merge.

## Recently closed

### Should visual search select the best candidate pool before chronological presentation?

`resolved` · `@evidence-intake-project.video.keyframe-candidate-selection-question/2`

Store::search_keyframes currently sorts every above-cut hit by still identifier and then truncates to the result limit. On long recordings, early weak matches can therefore crowd all later matches out. Should the kernel select the candidate pool by internal similarity (still never storing, printing or exporting the number) and then present that pool chronologically, return every above-cut hit with pagination, or use another recall-preserving rule? Resolve from the real-model benchmark because the answer depends on actual score distributions and a reviewer's practical result budget.

**Blocks**
- `proposed` [Choose the visual finder model by local body-camera retrieval recall](ACTIVE-WORK.md#choose-the-visual-finder-model-by-local-body-camera-retrieval-recall) `@evidence-intake-project.video.real-embedding-benchmark/1`

**Resolution.** Select the reviewer's bounded candidate pool by internal cosine similarity, then reorder that pool by still identifier for chronological presentation. Store, hits, JSON and exports still contain no score. Do not apply the synthetic 0.20 fixed cut: the first live SigLIP 2 run produced maxima of only 0.0766–0.1204 for nine representative queries, so the cut returned nothing. A no-match judgment remains the reviewer's; future human-labeled evaluation may add a pinned per-model stopping rule, but it must not restore early-timeline bias.
